probe:maskdiff.summary: P8 verdict: the OCT texture mask (18.05 cm3) and the MRI tissue mask (13.5 cm3 cleaned) do not describe the same object, and no rigid pose makes them coincide. At P_R5 (OCT space, cleaned MRI tissue) the OCT mask splits into A (agree) 8.60 cm3 = 48 %, B (OCT tissue / MRI background, inside the MRI FOV) 7.32 cm3 = 41 %, D (outside the MRI FOV) 2.13 cm3 = 12 %; the MRI tissue splits into A 64 %, C (MRI tissue / OCT not) 2.93 cm3 = 22 % (1.04 of it on OCT black tiles), E (outside the OCT box) 2.03 cm3 = 15 %. Dice 0.63. P_v1 is the same picture (B 6.97, C 3.55, D 1.88). B is ONE connected component spanning the whole block (bbox = the block, thickness up to 8.3 mm, 78 % further than 1 mm from A, 71 % within 2 mm of the OCT mask's outer boundary): in the MRI it is pure background (median 0.29, 94 % < 0.35, histogram identical to the agarose reference) while in the OCT it has the same intensity as A (17.0k), HIGHER texture F than A (median 0.0239 vs 0.0205; agarose outside the mask 0.0080) and a mask-boundary rim strength equal to A's (73 % vs 75 % above A's p25). Neither threshold explains it: MRI thr 0.45/0.541/0.65 leaves B at 7.26/7.32/7.34 and C at 2.98/2.93/2.89 (0.35 floods the agarose: 39.5 cm3); raising the OCT GMM threshold 20 % shrinks the mask 14 % (19.5 -> 16.8 cm3 in my rebuild) but only moves 0.94 cm3 from B into C (B 7.75 -> 6.81, C 2.53 -> 3.46), and at +50 % (12.3 cm3, the MRI volume) B is still 5.2 and C 5.9 - the weakly textured voxels are preferentially in A, not in B. Rigid pose changes: the only 1-D direction that helps is translation along OCT y (-7 mm: Dice 0.65 -> 0.71, B 7.23 -> 6.01, C_valid 1.87 -> 1.59); rotations of +-40 deg about any OCT axis change Dice by <= 0.04 (the rotation ambiguity every probe saw); the greedy rigid Dice optimum (64 deg / 26 mm block-corner away, anatomically wrong - the MRI fibre pattern is rotated relative to the OCT's) reaches only Dice 0.75 with B 5.47, C_valid 1.61, D 1.92. So <= 1.9 cm3 of B (25 %) is pose-attributable and >= 5.5 cm3 (75 % of B, 30 % of the OCT mask) is OCT-mask material that has no MRI tissue at ANY rigid pose. Looking at the images: that material is (i) a 2-3 mm shell of striped, rim-less agarose around most of the mask boundary (B is 60 % of the mask's outer 2 mm), (ii) folded lamellar sheets at the top of the block (the 'petal' structure, partly in D) whose enclosed pockets the mask's pocket/hole-filling rules turned into mask, and (iii) on one side the OCT body's fibre texture continuing 3-5 mm past the MRI body outline (the pose part), mirrored by C#2 on the opposite (y-) side where the MRI body extends 4-6 mm beyond a clean bright OCT rim. C is two components: the MRI cerebellar folia lobe (1.49 cm3, 49 % on black tiles, F ~0 elsewhere - no OCT counterpart at either pose: a displaced/undissected piece) and the y- body extension (1.38 cm3, MRI 0.86 fibre tissue on OCT agarose beyond a real rim: pose shift and/or MRI brain beyond the dissection cut); at the MRI surface off the OCT mask the OCT shows no rim (36 % vs 75 %). MRI truncation accounts for D (2.1 cm3) + 0.34 cm3 of B (within 0.5 mm of a crop face); the MRI specimen touches 3 crop faces.
probe:maskdiff.recipe: Server work/probe_xr/maskdiff/, CPU only (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES empty, 4 threads, specimen.py workers 4). Three scripts, all reusing octreg.common (resample_to_grid / grid_points / pool_mean_np / pooled_affine) and octreg.specimen (_run/_field_chunk/_rim_chunk/gmm2_1d/cleanup/grid_coords/ball): (1) p8_maskdiff.py --phases regions,texture,comps,thresh,figs. Data work/v11/xiangrui_I58bs (oct150 destriped 0.15 mm, oct150_mask = texture mask, mri 0.08 mm, mri_tissue raw threshold 0.541). MRI tissue cleaned exactly as qc_fine.clean_mask (closing ball 2 vox + fill holes + components >= 1 mm3): 13.315 -> 13.508 cm3, 2 components (13.502 + 0.006 cm3: the cerebellum is attached to the body in the MRI, so 'pieces' could not separate brainstem/cerebellum; done visually). Poses P_R5 = runs/v11/xiangrui_I58bs/T_oct2mri_structural.npy (== final T), P_v1 = runs/xiangrui_I58bs_novasc/T_oct2mri.npy (det 0.93). OCT space: MRI intensity / cleaned+raw tissue / piece label resampled onto the 0.15 mm OCT grid through P (trilinear > 0.5, pieces nearest); inMRI = OCT voxel centre maps inside the MRI array; d_face = distance to the nearest MRI FOV face (mm). Regions: A = Mo & Mm; B = Mo & ~Mm & inMRI; C = ~Mo & Mm (split C_valid = oct150 > 0, C_tile = black tiles); D = Mo & ~inMRI. MRI space (cross-check): OCT mask and validity resampled onto the 0.08 mm MRI grid through inv(P); inOCT = MRI voxel centre inside the OCT box; E = Mm & ~inOCT. Components: scipy label with 26-connectivity on B and C; per component volume, centroid (OCT ijk, MRI mm, MRI ijk), bbox, max thickness (2 x max EDT), oct150 / F / MRI-via-P percentiles, MRI fraction < 0.35 and 0.35-0.541, black-tile fraction, distance to tiles (EDT of oct150 > 0, box faces excluded), to MRI faces, to OCT box faces (+ nearest face name z-/z+/y-/y+/x-/x+), distance to A (median, p90, fraction <= 0.45 mm = boundary blur), nearest MRI piece. References: tissue = A, agarose = valid & ~Mo & ~Mm & inMRI. Texture: F rebuilt with specimen.py's own workers from the saved octv (BP 0.08 mm, std window 0.36 mm, W grid 0.16 mm, smoothing 0.48 mm) and rim strength E likewise; GMM threshold on log F; masks re-derived with the pipeline's marker opening / watershed on E / enclosed-pocket rule / cleanup / resample-to-0.15 at thr x {0.8, 1.0, 1.2, 1.5}; F resampled to 0.15 mm (F150). MRI thresholds 0.35 / 0.45 / 0.541 / 0.65: raw and cleaned volumes, then A/B/C at P_R5 with the cleaned mask through P (also the raw mask and a direct 'MRI-via-P > thr' cross-check). Figures: 3 mid-mask planes x 2 poses in OCT space (OCT | MRI via P; A green, B red, C blue, D yellow, MRI FOV dashed, OCT mask orange) and in MRI space (MRI with regions | MRI with OCT mask via P orange and cleaned tissue cyan, OCT box dashed); close-ups (+-9 mm) of the 2 largest B and C components per pose: OCT | MRI via P | log10 F, component contour yellow. (2) p8_scan.py: B breakdown (fraction of B and A with F150 > k x 0.01514 for k = 1..3; B by distance to A; B and A by depth inside the OCT mask); Dice(OCT mask in FOV, cleaned MRI tissue on valid OCT) on a 0.3 mm pooled OCT grid: 1-D translations along the OCT array axes (-8..+8 mm, 1 mm) and rotations about the OCT axes through the A centroid (-40..+40 deg, 5 deg) from P_R5 and P_v1; greedy coordinate descent over 6 rigid parameters (steps 10/5/2.5/1/0.5 deg and 4/2/1/0.5/0.25 mm, ~300 evaluations) to the Dice optimum; regions re-evaluated at 0.15 mm at that pose; overview figure + landscape figure. (3) p8_rim.py: rim strength E on the 0.15 grid; OCT-mask boundary voxels (>= 3 vox from box faces, >= 2 from tiles) split by their region (A / B): E percentiles and fraction above A's p25; every B/A voxel assigned the E of its nearest usable boundary point; MRI-tissue boundary in OCT space split by on/off the OCT mask with E and a 0.6 mm local-max E. Jobs run detached (setsid) with logs /tmp/p8_a.log (regions+texture, 244 s), /tmp/p8_b.log (comps+thresh+figs, 104 s), /tmp/p8_c.log (scan, 251 s), /tmp/p8_d.log (rim, 9 s). Everything intermediate cached in work/probe_xr/maskdiff/cache/.

probe:maskdiff.caveats: 1. What the figures show (looked at all of them): OCT-space overviews (both poses): the brainstem body is green and its outline agrees on the left/bottom of the axis-0 plane; a large red band sits above/right of the body where the OCT shows folded lamellar sheets and striped smooth material and the MRI-via-P panel is pure noise; blue sits in the black-tile region (bottom-left) and along the y- side; the folded 'petal' structure at the top of the block is largely yellow (D, outside the MRI FOV). MRI-space overviews: the MRI is a whole-brain crop - the tissue touches three crop faces (i-, j-, j+), the cerebellar folia lobe (dark branching arbor) is bottom-left in the axis-2 plane and largely blue, and the OCT mask (orange) extends ~10 mm below the MRI tissue as a slab of MRI background. B1 close-up: at the A/B boundary on the body side the OCT fibre texture continues without any rim into B (pose part); in the axis-1 panel the red region is smooth with horizontal tile stripes and the mask boundary crosses it without a rim (agarose part); in the axis-0/2 panels the red region contains bright folded lamellae (membranes or folia) with agarose between them. C1 (P_R5): the MRI folia lobe lands on black tiles and a smooth low-F OCT patch. C2 (P_R5) / C1 (P_v1): the OCT body has a clean bright rim exactly at the mask boundary and striped agarose beyond it, while the MRI body continues 4-6 mm beyond that rim. Pdice figure: the shell of red around the whole mask persists and the MRI fibre pattern is visibly rotated relative to the OCT's - a mask-overlap optimum, not a registration. Landscape figure: only OCT-y translation has a slope; rotations are flat within 0.04 Dice. 2. The texture field F and rim strength E were rebuilt from the saved octv.npy, which is DESTRIPED; the prep computed the texture mask on the un-destriped octv (prep_subject.py line 192), so my GMM threshold is 0.01230 vs the prep's 0.01514 and my thr x 1.0 mask (19.55 cm3) differs from the prep mask (18.05, Dice 0.944). The +20 % sweep is therefore relative to my rebuild; the qualitative result (volume moves from B to C, disagreement not reduced) is robust across x 0.8-1.5. F150 statistics inside B use the prep threshold 0.01514 for the k x thr fractions. 3. F cannot arbitrate inside B independently: B is inside the texture mask, so it has F above threshold by construction (except pocket/hole-filled voxels); the rim test (E at the mask boundary) and the MRI intensity are the independent evidence. The 'membrane / lamellar sheets' reading of the folded structure is visual only; whether it is meninges, cerebellar folia or agarose layering was not verified. 4. MRI tissue used for the regions is the qc_fine-cleaned mask (closing 2 vox + fill + >= 1 mm3); raw-mask volumes are reported alongside (differences <= 0.07 cm3). The cleaned MRI tissue is a single connected component (13.502 cm3) plus a 0.006 cm3 speck, so the requested piece association (brainstem / cerebellum / small piece) could not be done by connectivity; the cerebellar lobe was identified visually from the folia pattern. The 'separate small tissue piece' was not identified in either modality. 5. C is reported with and without the black tiles (1.04 cm3 of C is on tiles = untestable); D and E are untestable by definition; 'MRI truncation' here means the crop FOV, and because the crop comes from a whole brain, C may also contain brain tissue that was never part of the dissected specimen (the mirror of truncation) - this cannot be separated from a pose error with these data. 6. The Dice scans are rigid only (no scale); the earlier probes' 25 % shrink would reduce B further but was already shown to be anatomically wrong. The greedy optimum is a mask-overlap optimum with ~300 evaluations at 0.3 mm; it is not unique (P_R5 and P_v1 starts reach different 64-65 deg poses with Dice 0.75-0.76) and no intensity measure (MI/NCC) was evaluated there. 7. 'inside MRI FOV' = the OCT voxel centre maps inside the MRI array; d_face is measured to the array faces, not to the cleaned tissue's 2-voxel erosion at the faces. 8. P_v1 is affine (det 0.93), so its MRI-space volumes are 7 % smaller than its OCT-space volumes. 9. Face names use OCT array axes (z = axis 0, y = axis 1, x = axis 2 = the physical sectioning axis); the 'y- side' of C#2 refers to the OCT array axis 1 face at index 0. 10. Run-time: ~10 min total CPU; nothing was written outside work/probe_xr/maskdiff/ and /tmp.
probe:maskdiff.verdict: The evidence supports 'agarose (non-MRI-tissue) kept by the OCT mask' as the dominant cause, with 'displaced/undissected pieces plus a several-mm pose error along OCT y' as a secondary cause, and rules out the MRI threshold entirely; MRI truncation is real but bookkept separately (D). Proportions of the OCT-mask mismatch (B + D = 9.45 cm3 at P_R5): ~5.5 cm3 (58 %; 30 % of the whole mask) is OCT-mask material with MRI background at every rigid pose tested - the outer 2-3 mm shell of the mask (B is 60 % of the mask's outer 2 mm, striped and rim-less in the OCT) plus lamellar sheets and the agarose pockets they enclose (the mask's enclosed-pocket rule and hole filling turn these into mask), texture-strong and rim-bounded in the OCT and therefore invisible to any F threshold (raising it moves volume into C instead); ~1.5-1.9 cm3 (16-20 %) is pose/displacement - the OCT body continues 3-5 mm past the MRI body outline on one side while the MRI body extends 4-6 mm beyond a clean OCT rim on the y- side (translation -4..-7 mm along OCT y is the only rigid direction that reduces the disagreement, the same direction MI and the surface probe pointed to), and the MRI cerebellar lobe (C#1, ~1.5 cm3, half on black tiles) has no OCT counterpart at either pose while the OCT's folded 'petal' structure has no MRI counterpart - a piece that is not rigidly co-located; ~2.1 cm3 (22 %) is MRI-crop truncation (D) + 0.34 cm3 face partial volume; 0 % is the MRI threshold (B 7.26-7.34 for thr 0.45-0.65, MRI in B 94 % < 0.35 = background). Concrete changes implied: (1) stop using the OCT texture mask boundary as a specimen surface in any objective (surface distance, Dice, overlap gates): at best 75 % Dice is reachable and only at an anatomically wrong pose, so the fine stage's failures to converge and the shrink/rotate runaways are a property of the masks, not the optimiser; keep m_spec = eroded (MRI tissue via T) & OCT mask (i.e. A eroded), which is the only region where both modalities agree; (2) tighten the OCT mask by an MRI-independent rule that targets the shell and the pockets rather than F: disable the enclosed-pocket reassignment and the 3-D hole filling in specimen.py (or accept pockets only when bounded by a rim), and require rim strength at the watershed boundary (E above the tissue-boundary p25) or erode the mask by ~2 mm before any boundary-based use - a 20 % threshold increase does not do this; (3) treat the MRI tissue mask as 'brain in the crop', not the specimen: mask out the cerebellar folia lobe (or model the cerebellum piece as a second rigid body) and exclude MRI tissue within ~1 mm of the three crop faces it touches; (4) test a translation of -3 to -5 mm along OCT y from P_R5 with the intensity measures on A-eroded before any further fine-stage work, since every independent measure agrees on that direction and the mask evidence shows the body outline off by ~4-5 mm on the y faces.

probe:pieces.summary: P7 answers both questions negatively. Q1: the I58bs MRI tissue is ONE connected piece (raw 13.32 cm3, cleaned 13.51; erosion by 0.5-3.0 mm never yields a second component >= 0.0001 cm3), so it was cut by a texture+brightness criterion into a brainstem body (9.35 cm3) and a folia-textured cerebellum cap (4.15 cm3); no separate small piece exists in the MRI (the OCT's lower pieces lie outside the MRI FOV). The fine objective restricted to the BODY piece does not converge any better than the union: from P_R5 with 8 restarts (3 mm / 5 deg) 0/8 restarts land within 1 mm of the best for rigid, similarity->affine, body, cerebellum and union alike (max pairwise spread 12-17 mm, median distance to the best 6-12 mm); the unperturbed body chain itself leaves P_R5 by 4.2 mm / 10.4 deg (rigid). The body objective has at least three recurrent basins 6-8 mm / 6-17 deg from P_R5 (B: shift z,y,x = +1.5,-0.5,+1.9 mm, 15-17 deg, NCC 0.18-0.20 vs 0.11-0.13 near P_R5, MI32 0.093 vs 0.077; D: -2,+4.2,+3 mm, 6-8 deg, NCC 0.13-0.14; C from P_v1: -1,-1,-5.3 mm, 15 deg). Basin B is a genuine rigid local optimum (restarts of 1.5 mm/3 deg from it: 5/7 within 1 mm, largest cluster 7/9 with 1.5 mm diameter; landscapes unimodal in translation/rotation), but qc_fine rejects it: rim medians fwd 2.77 / rev 1.27 mm (P_R5 2.02 / 1.05), deep end 2.38/2.51 (2.18/1.98), only 48 % of the MRI boundary inside the OCT block, MI32 argmax at every range end; in the figure the MRI body outline hugs the OCT's upper-left rim in the 6-14 mm planes but is rotated ~15 deg so 3-5 mm of OCT tissue on the right/bottom lies outside the MRI, the bright cerebellar folia land on OCT with no folia texture, and the OCT's lower pieces (19-23 mm) have no MRI counterpart. The cerebellum piece cannot be fitted at all: through P_R5 its 1.3 mm-eroded mask overlaps the OCT specimen by only 0.24 cm3 (8.8k voxels; polarity guard has 0 blocks), its 'optimum' is 11 mm / 25 deg away with the MRI outline cutting diagonally through the OCT body. The body-cerebellum best-pose difference (6.8 mm / 15 deg rigid, 8.1 / 13 rsa) is smaller than the within-piece restart scatter (13-17 mm), so there is no evidence that the pieces want different affines - the objective pins nothing. Start independence fails: best body poses from P_R5 and P_v1 are 9.6 mm / 21 deg apart (rigid), 12.8 / 26 (rsa), and the P_v1 basin is the worst on the outline (rev 2.09, deep 3.6 mm). Q2: no evidence that the 20 um spacing along OCT array axis 2 (x) is wrong. The P_R5-centred sweep is dominated by basin hopping (rigid re-optimisation moves 4-11 mm at every s). Centred on the rigid body optimum, the full-mask NCC rises monotonically with +x stretch to the +0.5 range end, but n_spec falls 170k -> 118k (the stretched block's x ends leave the MRI tissue) and on a fixed central band (in-tissue fraction 0.99-1.00 at all s) the pure x profile peaks at +0.04..+0.08 (NCC 0.247 -> 0.249 at +0.1, MI32 0.167), the affine fits leave the x stretch at -0.01..+0.08, and MI/outline show no consistent x optimum: implied spacing 20.8-21.6 um, i.e. unchanged within ~5 %. The unexpected signal is on the CONTROL axis 0 (z): full-mask profiles prefer +0.08..+0.10, affine fits in basin B +0.10..+0.17, the central band +0.29..+0.35 (NCC and MI, both centres) - a 1.1-1.4x stretch preference along z (exp 0.3 = 1.35, a refractive-index-sized factor) that deserves a metadata check; along y the band prefers a 0.6-0.7x shrink (the P5/P6 shrink degeneracy) while the full mask prefers +0.2, so the sweep is not a clean spacing detector on y/z.
probe:pieces.recipe:
All on the AutoDL server in work/probe_xr/pieces/ (GPU RTX 4090, one process at a time; data work/v11/xiangrui_I58bs; P_R5 = work/runs/v11/xiangrui_I58bs/T_oct2mri_structural.npy, P_v1 = work/runs/xiangrui_I58bs_novasc/T_oct2mri.npy).
1. p7_pieces.py (CPU): clean the MRI tissue exactly as qc_fine (binary_closing ball 2 vox + fill_holes + components >= 1 mm3) -> tissue_clean.npy; EDT with padded faces (fine.erode_ball convention); for r in 0.5,1,1.5,2,2.5,3 mm: components of EDT >= r, seeds >= 0.3 cm3, geodesic reconstruction = skimage watershed on a flat image restricted to the tissue (competitive masked dilation) -> piece_labels_r*.npy + pieces_r*.png. Result: a single seed at every r, so no split.
2. Fallback cut, p7_feat.py + p7_cut2.py: interior-only features (EDT >= 0.3 mm, excluding the partial-volume rind that made a naive local-std Otsu cut (p7_cut.py, pieces_tex.png) label a 1-2 mm rind as 'cerebellum'): I10 = masked Gaussian (1 mm) intensity, S = masked local std in a 5-vox box smoothed 0.5 mm (reference boxes: cerebellum I10 1.234 / S 0.127, body 1.047 / 0.102; the I10 histogram has a second mode at 1.2-1.35). Folia score F = 0.5 (I10-1)/0.2 + 0.5 (S-0.10)/0.04; cerebellum seeds = (I10 > 1.18) & (S > 0.115) components >= 0.05 cm3 (0.658 + 0.162 + 0.057 cm3); body seed = largest component of (EDT >= 2.5 mm) minus a 1.5 mm neighbourhood of the folia (5.14 cm3); watershed of -F inside the tissue (rind flooded last) -> piece_labels_tex2.npy (uint8, 0.08 mm; 1 body, 2 cereb), pieces_tex2.json/png (3 axes x 8 slices, checked by eye: cyan = folia cap at low axis-0/axis-2 indices plus the thin slab; a few bright body-rind strips go to 'cereb', removed anyway by the 1.3 mm fit erosion). An LDA plane between the labels (normal ijk [-0.833, 0.023, -0.553], 87 deg to the tissue long axis [-0.055, 0.975, 0.215]) only reaches 0.79 balanced accuracy, so a plane cut was not used.
3. p7_fit.py fit (GPU): levels built with octreg.fine.Level exactly as fine_stage (mri_box = whole MRI, 0.3 mm: OCT pooled x2 / MRI x4 = 0.32 mm; 0.15 mm: native OCT / MRI x2); per piece an eroded mask erode_ball(pooled piece, 1.3 mm) at each level; m_spec(T) = piece via T > 0.5 & OCT texture mask & eroded validity (= Level.spec_mask with the piece in place of t_m_er), re-derived at each level start; 'union' = the pipeline's own L.t_m_er. Objective = octreg.fine.FineRefiner (sign-corrected 3 mm-flattened masked NCC, delta about the start, Adam, refine_delta with clamp 0.15 / reg 0.5 per step, lrs 0.01/0.15/0.005/0.005 halved at 0.15 mm, MRI tissue sampled through T as detached weight); sign = polarity_guard at P_R5 (-1 for body and union; cerebellum guard has 0 blocks -> -1 assumed). DOF 'rigid' = rigid 200 it at 0.3 then 200 at 0.15; 'rsa' = rigid 150 -> similarity 100 -> affine 200 at 0.3, affine 200 at 0.15 (fine.py's chained relative clamp). Chains: unperturbed + 8 restarts built with refine.compose from params_from_matrix(T_start): 5 deg about a random axis, 3 mm in a random direction, log-scale U(-0.03,0.03)/axis for rsa and 0 for rigid (seed 7, identical everywhere). Per chain: NCC with the chain's own final mask, NCC on the piece's fixed P_R5 point set at 0.15 mm (FineRefiner built at P_R5, evaluate_T), fine.MI32 on the piece's and the union's P_R5 point sets (edges fixed at P_R5), fine.pose_move vs P_R5 (block-corner mean, delta rotation) plus centre shift along the OCT axes and log-stretch of the delta along the OCT axes; clusters from the 9x9 block-corner distance matrix (n within 0.5 / 1 mm of the best-common-NCC chain, single-linkage 1 mm). Configs: body/cereb/union x rigid/rsa from P_R5, body x rigid/rsa from P_v1 (fit.json); then body/union rigid from the best body pose with 1.5 mm / 3 deg (fit_from_best_small.json) and body rigid/rsa with 3 mm / 5 deg (fit_from_best_large.json); p7_fit.py landscape = fine.landscape of the piece NCC and MI32 at P_R5, P_v1 and the best body poses (trans 1-6 mm, rot 2-20 deg, log-scale 0.05-0.5).
4. QC: p7_fit.py qcprep writes run_<cfg>/ (T_oct2mri = best pose, T_oct2mri_structural = T_oct2mri_prefine = P_R5 so the dashed-orange outline is P_R5, result.json copied from the v11 run) and octreg/scripts/qc_fine.py --work work/v11/xiangrui_I58bs --run <dir> --out qc_<cfg> for body_rigid_R5, body_rsa_R5, body_rigid_v1, cereb_rigid_R5, union_rigid_R5; PNGs downloaded and inspected.
5. p7_fit.py sweep: body piece, rigid, 0.3 mm level, 100 it, unperturbed + 2 restarts (2 mm / 3 deg): T_s = C @ fine.perturb_matrix('lscale', u_axis, s, c_o) for s = -0.5..0.5 step 0.1, axes x (2), z (0), y (1); at the best of the 3 chains: NCC (mask at pose and fixed centre mask), MI32 (mask at pose with edges fixed at C; fixed centre mask; union mask), qc_fine boundary fwd/rev rim medians from a verbatim port of qc_fine's Q1 with cached EDTs (validated: 2.0177 / 1.0543 at P_R5 = qc_fine.json), n_spec, rigid move from the scaled start. Run with C = P_R5 (sweep.json) and C = best body rigid pose (sweep_b7.json). p7_fit.py sweep_eval: coverage-free check - NCC/MI32 on the fixed middle third of the body m_spec along the swept axis, at the converged and at the pure scaled poses (sweep_b7_band.json, sweep_R5_band.json). Curves plotted locally (p7_summary.py, dl/sweep_curves*.png, copied to the server dir).

probe:pieces.caveats: 1. The body/cerebellum split is a texture+brightness cut, not an anatomical label: erosion never separates the tissue (a single seed at every r up to 3 mm), the LDA plane between the labels only reaches 0.79 balanced accuracy (not planar), a few bright textured body-rind strips are labelled cerebellum, and the folia fragments at the far end are cerebellum by construction; the 1.3 mm fit erosion removes most of the thin folia cap (4.15 -> 0.56-0.76 cm3) and only 0.24 cm3 of that overlaps the OCT specimen at P_R5, so every cerebellum fit is on 8.8k-49k voxels with an unrunnable polarity guard (sign -1 assumed) - those chains are reported but meaningless. 2. 'Converged NCC' with the chain's own mask is not comparable across chains (m_spec is re-derived at each level start from the chain's pose, the same mask-follows-pose degeneracy P5/P6 found); the best chain and the cluster tables use the NCC on the piece's fixed P_R5 point set, and both are reported; MI32 numbers are fine.MI32 on the 0.15 mm level with edges fixed at P_R5 and are not comparable with qc_fine's raw-MRI MI32. 3. Rigid-DOF restarts carry no log-scale perturbation (a rigid optimiser cannot undo it and it would inflate cluster radii by construction); rsa restarts use +-0.03. 4. As in fine.py, the 0.15 clamp is relative per step and chained (rigid -> sim -> affine -> affine), so cumulative log-stretches of +-0.17..0.24 occurred in the rsa runs (P5 caveat 3). 5. The union piece is the pipeline's raw-tissue erosion (8.42 cm3 at 0.3 mm) while the pieces come from the cleaned tissue and lose their cut face to the erosion (body+cereb 6.52); this does not affect the conclusions (the union behaves like the body). 6. The sweep's rigid re-optimisation hops basins (moves 1-11 mm), so the P_R5-centred curves say little; the band evaluation removes the coverage effect but depends on the band choice (middle third) and it produces an implausible 0.6-0.7x shrink preference along y and a 1.3-1.4x stretch along z, so the only robust Q2 statement is the axis-2 null (three independent measures agree on +0.04..+0.08); the axis-0 (z) stretch preference is consistent in sign across all measures but its size ranges from +0.08 (full mask) to +0.35 (band) and should be checked against the acquisition metadata (which array axis is the optical depth axis; P3 identified axis 2 as the sectioning axis) rather than taken from this sweep. 7. The qc_fine boundary at the sweep poses uses my verbatim port (validated to 4 decimals at P_R5 and P_v1), whole-tissue definition; no piece-restricted outline measure was computed. 8. Only one GPU process ran at a time, OMP_NUM_THREADS=4; nothing was written outside work/probe_xr/pieces and /tmp; the earlier probes' P_R3/I58bs_s40 prep is a different prep than the native v1.1 prep used here (numbers are not directly comparable with wf3 values). 9. The union_rigid_R5 QC was not inspected by eye (its pose is 1.7 mm / 3.7 deg from the body pose and its qc numbers are identical to 3 decimals).
probe:pieces.verdict: The evidence supports neither 'the pieces need different affines' nor 'the sectioning-axis spacing is wrong'; it supports the mask/content-mismatch explanation of the earlier probes: the fine objective does not pin the pose on the brainstem body alone any more than on the union (0/8 restarts within 1 mm for every piece and DOF from P_R5; >= 3 recurrent basins 6-8 mm / 6-17 deg apart whose NCC is higher than at P_R5 but whose outline agreement is worse, fwd rim 2.5-2.9 mm vs 2.0), the MRI cerebellum piece barely overlaps the OCT specimen (0.24 cm3 at P_R5, so no piece-specific affine can be estimated and its 'pose' is anatomically wrong), and the body-cerebellum pose difference (6.8 mm / 15 deg) is smaller than the within-piece restart scatter (13-17 mm). Along OCT array axis 2 the coverage-free profiles, the affine fits and MI all put the scale optimum within +0.04..+0.08 (20.8-21.6 um): keep the 20 um metadata. Concrete changes: (a) do not add piecewise affines; (b) drop the cerebellum from the MRI side of the specimen mask (piece_labels_tex2.npy) and, more importantly, stop re-deriving m_spec from the current pose inside the fine stage - optimise on a FIXED body-core OCT point set chosen once at the reference pose with a fixed tissue weight, because the mask-follows-pose mechanism is what rewards the 6-8 mm / 15 deg basins; then re-test restart convergence, and if it still fails treat the fine stage on I58bs as a <= 1 mm / 2 deg polish from P_R5 with 1 mm / 2 deg restarts rather than a 3 mm / 5 deg search (the rigid basin capture radius measured here is ~1.5 mm / 3 deg); (c) before any further tuning, check the OCT voxel spacing / refractive-index handling along array axis 0, where every measure prefers a +0.08..+0.35 log-scale stretch (exp 0.3 = 1.35), and confirm with the acquisition metadata which array axis is the optical depth axis.
